payload.text: A physical pendulum of mass M has pivot-to-center distance d and moment of inertia I about the pivot.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Predict how the observable changes when the defining scale parameter is doubled, and justify the prediction quantitatively.

criteria.description: Doubling d (holding I and M fixed) changes T=2π√(I/Mgd) by a factor of 1/√2, so the period decreases to T/√2, since T∝1/√d.
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how the T∝1/√d dependence in T=2π√(I/Mgd), given the assumption that I and M are unchanged as d changes, justifies why doubling d divides the period by √2.

criteria.description: Explain how the T∝1/√d dependence in T=2π√(I/Mgd), given the assumption that I and M are unchanged as d changes, justifies why doubling d divides the period by √2.
required_evidence: I and M held fixed as d changes
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.
